source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

title: How do footballers cope with high-pressure scenarios?

lines.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
lines.zh: 哈囉。這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。

lines.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 我是 Georgie。我是 Neil。

lines.en: Neil, I'm not a huge fan of football, but I know you are.
lines.zh: Neil，我不太熱衷足球，但我知道你很愛。

lines.en: So why do you love it so much?
lines.zh: 你為什麼這麼喜歡足球？

lines.en: Oh, where can I start?
lines.zh: 喔，該從哪裡說起呢？

lines.en: I think it's the combination of the passion and also the skill and athleticism of the players.
lines.zh: 我想是熱情，加上球員的技巧和運動能力，這些結合在一起。

lines.en: Um, they call it 'the beautiful game' for a reason.
lines.zh: 嗯，大家稱它為「美麗的運動」是有原因的。

lines.en: Now, football players are faster than ever before, but the game is also about making very quick decisions.
lines.zh: 現在的足球員速度比以往都快，但這項運動同時也和快速做決定有關。

lines.en: Yes, to be the best of the best, some football clubs have started looking beyond the body, to the brain.
lines.zh: 對，為了成為頂尖中的頂尖，有些足球俱樂部開始不只看身體，還把目光放到大腦上。

lines.en: Here's Tom Cooke, academy psychologist for Nottingham Forest Football Club, talking to the BBC World Service.
lines.zh: 這是諾丁漢森林足球俱樂部青訓學院的心理師 Tom Cooke 對 BBC 世界廣播說的話。

lines.en: We're watching these athletes make decisions in split instincts under the highest pressures and the highest intensities.
lines.zh: 我們看著這些運動員在最高的壓力、最高的強度下，憑著瞬間的直覺做決定。

lines.en: It made a lot of sense to go, well, neurologically or cognitively, there's something going on.
lines.zh: 這讓人很自然地想到：嗯，在神經或認知層面上，一定有什麼事正在發生。

lines.en: There's something going on in the brain when the athletes are making quick decisions.
lines.zh: 運動員快速做決定時，大腦裡有某些事正在發生。

lines.en: If there's something going on, something unknown and interesting is happening.
lines.zh: 如果「there's something going on」，就表示有某件未知而有趣的事正在發生。

lines.en: So what's happening inside the brains of football players?
lines.zh: 那麼，足球員的大腦裡到底發生了什麼事？

lines.en: And could brain training help win more games?
lines.zh: 大腦訓練能幫助贏得更多比賽嗎？

lines.en: That's what we'll be hearing about in this programme.
lines.zh: 這就是我們在這集節目中要聽到的內容。

lines.en: And don't forget to find a free transcript at bbclearningenglish.com But first Neil, I have a question for you.
lines.zh: 別忘了到 bbclearningenglish.com 找免費的逐字稿。不過首先，Neil，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: As we've heard, football players have to make decisions in high-pressure situations and their performance may be influenced by their emotional state and fear response.
lines.zh: 就像我們剛剛聽到的，足球員必須在高壓情況下做決定，他們的表現可能會受到情緒狀態和恐懼反應的影響。

lines.en: But which part of the brain is best known for its role in processing fear and detecting threats?
lines.zh: 那麼，大腦的哪個部位最為人所知的是負責處理恐懼和偵測威脅？

lines.en: Is it a) the brain stem, b) the amygdala, or c) the cerebellum?
lines.zh: 是：a) 腦幹、b) 杏仁核，還是 c) 小腦？

lines.en: Well, I don't know.
lines.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

lines.en: But I'm going to guess b) the amygdala because I like the sound of the word.
lines.zh: 不過我要猜 b) 杏仁核，因為我喜歡這個字的發音。

lines.en: OK. Well I'll reveal the answer later in the programme.
lines.zh: 好。我會在節目稍後揭曉答案。

lines.en: In 2014, a group of Japanese scientists studied the brain of Brazilian football star Neymar.
lines.zh: 2014 年，一群日本科學家研究了巴西足球明星內馬爾的大腦。

lines.en: They found that his brain was a lot less active than the brains of his peers when he rotated his right ankle.
lines.zh: 他們發現，他轉動右腳踝時，大腦的活躍程度比同儕低很多。

lines.en: Here's Holly Bridge, professor of neuroscience at the University of Oxford, talking about this research to the BBC World Service.
lines.zh: 這是牛津大學神經科學教授 Holly Bridge 向 BBC 世界廣播談這項研究。

lines.en: That reduction in activity in Neymar's cortex reflects that he has absolute expertise in moving his feet, and it's essentially done with very, very little conscious effort. Holly said Neymar has absolute expertise in moving his feet.
lines.zh: 內馬爾大腦皮質活動量的減少，反映出他在移動雙腳這件事上有絕對的專業能力，基本上幾乎不用刻意費力就能做到。Holly 說內馬爾在移動雙腳上有絕對的專業能力。

lines.en: Expertise means a high level of skill or knowledge gained with experience.
lines.zh: Expertise 是指透過經驗累積的高水準技能或知識。

lines.en: Neymar's expertise is shown without much conscious effort.
lines.zh: 內馬爾的專業能力展現出來時，幾乎不需要刻意費力。

lines.en: Conscious describes something done with awareness, not by accident.
lines.zh: Conscious 形容某件事是有意識地去做的，不是意外。

lines.en: So if Neymar kicks the ball without much conscious effort, he plays without thinking too much.
lines.zh: 所以如果內馬爾踢球時不太需要刻意費力，就代表他比賽時不用想太多。

lines.en: Decades after this research, football clubs are becoming more interested in brain data technology, even exploring whether a player's brain can be trained.
lines.zh: 在這項研究的多年之後，足球俱樂部對大腦數據科技越來越有興趣，甚至在探索球員的大腦能不能被訓練。

lines.en: Here's Tom Cooke, academy psychologist for Nottingham Forest Football Club.
lines.zh: 這是諾丁漢森林足球俱樂部青訓學院的心理師 Tom Cooke。

lines.en: What we're doing is trying to design sessions but with cognition or neuroscience at the centre of it.
lines.zh: 我們在做的，是試著設計以認知或神經科學為核心的訓練課程。

lines.en: So it could be something like they're not great at storing lots of information.
lines.zh: 比方說，可能是他們不太擅長記住大量資訊。

lines.en: So we're trying to overwhelm them in a safe environment like training.
lines.zh: 所以我們試著在像訓練這樣安全的環境中，讓他們承受超出負荷的資訊量。

lines.en: That's the way the development and improvement can happen to hopefully affect when they go out into games or cup competitions.
lines.zh: 這樣就能帶來發展與進步，希望在他們上場比賽或參加盃賽時發揮作用。

lines.en: Training can help players deal with the pressures of the game.
lines.zh: 訓練可以幫助球員應對比賽的壓力。

lines.en: Here's Holly Bridge again talking about how emotions can affect a player's game.
lines.zh: 這是 Holly Bridge 再次談到情緒如何影響球員的表現。

lines.en: A lot of performance is also driven by your emotional state, and that is something you can learn to control.
lines.zh: 很多表現也是由你的情緒狀態所驅動的，而這是你可以學著控制的。

lines.en: How well a player performs is driven by their emotional state. Here, driven by means influenced by or pushed forward by.
lines.zh: 球員表現得好不好，是由情緒狀態驅動的。這裡的 driven by 意思是受到～影響或被～推動。

lines.en: Holly says that too many emotions can lead to a lack of precision and focus.
lines.zh: Holly 說，情緒太多會導致缺乏精準度和專注力。

lines.en: In a football match, high-pressure scenarios like penalties, corners and free kicks offer rare moments of stillness.
lines.zh: 在足球比賽中，罰球、角球和自由球這些高壓場景，提供了難得的靜止時刻。

lines.en: Here's Niklas Häusler, founder and CEO of Neuro 11, talking to the BBC World Service.
lines.zh: 這是 Neuro 11 的創辦人兼執行長 Niklas Häusler 對 BBC 世界廣播說的話。

lines.en: He measures players' brainwaves before these important kicks and teaches them how to stay relaxed.
lines.zh: 他在這些重要的踢球前測量球員的腦波，並教他們如何保持放鬆。

lines.en: If you don't focus right in those moments and let's say mentally you're all over the place, then it becomes more difficult to have an accurate corner and to try to win the game.
lines.zh: 如果你在那些時刻沒辦法好好專注，比方說心裡亂成一團，那就更難踢出精準的角球、更難贏得比賽。

lines.en: And when we talk about margins, those are the little margins that can make all the difference.
lines.zh: 當我們談到差距時，就是這些小小的差距可以決定一切。

lines.en: If you're mentally all over the place, it's more difficult to kick the ball accurately.
lines.zh: 如果你心裡亂成一團，就更難把球踢得精準。

lines.en: When we describe something as all over the place, we mean that it's chaotic, disorganised, or confused.
lines.zh: 當我們形容某件事 all over the place，意思是它很混亂、沒有條理或讓人困惑。

lines.en: Niklas said that small margins can make all the difference to a game.
lines.zh: Niklas 說，小小的差距可以決定一場比賽的結果。

lines.en: Yes, a margin is a measure of difference.
lines.zh: 對，margin 是衡量差距的量。

lines.en: Here we're talking about small details that can affect a player's performance or outcome of a match.
lines.zh: 這裡我們談的是可能影響球員表現或比賽結果的小細節。

lines.en: Now, speaking of how emotions can affect performance, I think it's time for the answer to your quiz question, Georgie.
lines.zh: 說到情緒如何影響表現，Georgie，我想該揭曉你的問題答案了。

lines.en: Yes, I asked you which part of the brain is best known for its role in processing fear.
lines.zh: 對，我問你大腦的哪個部位最為人所知的是負責處理恐懼。

lines.en: And I guessed b) the amygdala.
lines.zh: 我猜的是 b) 杏仁核。

lines.en: Which was the correct answer. Well done.
lines.zh: 這就是正確答案。答得好。

lines.en: The amygdala is associated with our processing of fear and anxiety.
lines.zh: 杏仁核和我們處理恐懼與焦慮有關。

lines.en: OK, time for a vocabulary recap.
lines.zh: 好，詞彙複習時間。

lines.en: If there is something going on, something interesting or important is happening.
lines.zh: 如果 there is something going on，就是有某件有趣或重要的事正在發生。

lines.en: Expertise is specialised knowledge or skill gained through study or experience.
lines.zh: Expertise 是透過學習或經驗獲得的專業知識或技能。

lines.en: Conscious means involving active thought or attention.
lines.zh: Conscious 的意思是涉及主動的思考或注意力。

lines.en: If something is driven by something, it is influenced by it and pushed forward by it.
lines.zh: 如果某件事 driven by 某件事，就是受到它影響、被它推動。

lines.en: All over the place describes a situation or mental state which is disorganised, chaotic, or confused.
lines.zh: All over the place 形容一個混亂、沒有條理或困惑的情況或心理狀態。

lines.en: And finally, a margin is a measure of difference, small details of which can affect an outcome.
lines.zh: 最後，margin 是衡量差距的量，其中的小細節可能影響結果。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember you can find a free transcript, worksheet and quiz on our website, bbclearningenglish.com Goodbye for now. Goodbye.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，但別忘了，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有免費的逐字稿、學習單和測驗。先說再見了。再見。
